Tonight-ish. Look through the telescope if you're feeling brave. Or foolish. They're the same muscle.

Ottoline Marsh finished her map of the drowned stars and taught us to read them. She says you can't mend the old sun — but maybe you can make a small one, close by, that belongs to everybody. I can't stop thinking about it.
Through the great glass: seven small lights, and the dark between them, which is not as empty as it looks.
Through the great glass: cloud, cloud, and the faint hum of something very far away. Ottoline's chart has gaps in it.
Through the great glass: one star, much brighter than the rest, getting brighter.
It is not getting brighter. It is getting _closer_.
Well! I'll be updating the chapter on falling stars. It'll be mostly exclamation marks.
Have these spectacles. Mine. They make you notice things. Dreadful habit, noticing.
